chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd Allah al-Halabi said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman who gave birth from adultery (zina), should I take her as a wet-nurse?' He said, 'Do not have her nurse (your child), nor her daughter.'

key_terms.تَسْتَرْضِعْهَا: To have her nurse (your child) / to take her as a wet-nurse
key_terms.ظِئْراً: Wet-nurse (specifically one who nurses an infant)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking a woman who gave birth from zina as a wet-nurse and her daughter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on wet-nursing (radāʿ) for a woman who gave birth from illicit intercourse (zina). He explicitly states that one should neither take her nor her daughter as wet-nurses, indicating that the child of zina and her offspring are excluded from the legal effects of radāʿ that establish kinship (muḥādarah). This ruling highlights the distinct status of children of zina in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital prohibitions derived from nursing.
